processes.title: Assemble-to-Order / Assembly Processing
processes.memory_hook: The sales order does not wait for MRP to notice it; it can create the assembly object immediately.
processes.deployment_scope: SAP S/4HANA / Private Edition; classic assembly-processing model documented for 2025 FPS01.
processes.business_intent: Create customer-specific supply directly from the sales order when production, planned-order or network execution must start immediately and the confirmed date depends on component availability and assembly scheduling.

control_plane.why: decides whether the sales item triggers assembly processing and which assembly object is created
controls a static 1:1 link or a dynamic planned-order-to-production-order path
turns production feasibility into the customer-confirmed delivery date

data_hinges.changes: whether the sales order creates the intended assembly object
what must be assembled and how long it takes
the earliest feasible committed customer date

impact_summary: Sales and Production are coupled earlier than in ordinary MTO: order creation can immediately create the production-side object.
A quantity/date change can propagate into the assembly object, so change governance becomes part of sales-order design.
constraints: Classic assembly processing is deployment-specific; do not describe it as a universal Public Cloud sales-order behavior.
A tight 1:1 link gives fast promise feedback but also makes late commercial changes expensive.
lead_questions: Why choose direct assembly processing instead of ordinary MTO with an MRP run?
Which object is created: production order, planned order or network, and why?
How do component shortages move the customer confirmation date?

processes.title: Engineer-to-Order / Sales from Project Stock
processes.memory_hook: MTO is tied to the sales order. ETO is tied to the project that exists because of the customer order.
processes.deployment_scope: SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608 and SAP S/4HANA project-manufacturing scenarios.
processes.business_intent: Engineer, procure and manufacture customer-specific products against a WBS element when project structure, project stock, project controlling and engineering changes are part of fulfillment.

control_plane.why: moves the supply and cost object from the normal sales-order segment into project context
creates project-specific MRP segments and individual requirements
decides when the product structure is ready enough for procurement and production

data_hinges.changes: stock ownership segment, MRP planning context, costs and profitability attribution
how inventory and production variances are valued and reported
whether BOM/routing changes are still allowed and whether execution can start

impact_summary: The sales order remains the customer contract, but project/WBS becomes the execution and cost backbone.
Production and procurement can both supply project stock; the important boundary is the WBS, not the manufacturing technology.
constraints: ETO is heavier than ordinary MTO. Use the project layer when engineering, project stock, project controlling or lot-size-one governance justify it.
Engineering changes after procurement or production starts require explicit revision and impact control.
lead_questions: What makes this ETO rather than ordinary MTO?
Where are stock and costs collected: sales order or WBS?
How do engineering changes propagate into open procurement and production?

processes.title: Engineer-to-Order for Complex Assembly / CTO+
processes.memory_hook: Configuration chooses the product. CTO+ still lets engineering change how this one customer product is built.
processes.deployment_scope: SAP S/4HANA 2025 FPS01, Production Engineering and Operations for Complex Assembly. Treat availability as deployment-specific.
processes.business_intent: Fulfil a configured customer order when standard variant configuration is not enough and the manufacturing BOM or shop-floor routing needs customer-specific engineering changes.

control_plane.why: provides the customer-specific starting configuration before engineering changes begin
creates the engineering workspace that joins the manufacturing BOM and shop-floor routing for the order-specific product
separates a design that may still change from a structure that production can execute

control_plane.control: change impact on components and operations
control_plane.why: keeps order-specific engineering changes aligned with procurement and shop-floor execution

data_hinges.changes: which product options form the starting point for the individual design
the customer-specific component structure used for manufacturing
the customer-specific production steps and component assignments
whether downstream procurement and production may safely proceed

impact_summary: This is deeper than normal variant configuration: engineering can adapt the order-specific production structure after the customer configuration already exists.
A late commercial change can become an engineering, procurement and production change, so impact analysis matters more than simple sales-order copy control.
constraints: Do not present CTO+ as a generic S/4HANA Sales feature; it belongs to a specific complex-assembly production architecture.
Use ordinary MTO or standard configurable MTO when a reusable BOM/routing and standard configuration already describe the product well enough.
lead_questions: What requirement cannot be solved by standard variant configuration alone?
Which object is the engineering source of truth after the sales order is configured?
When is the order-specific BOM/routing stable enough for procurement and production?
How do we assess a late sales change against already released engineering and execution objects?

processes.title: Sales Order Processing – Project-Based Services
processes.memory_hook: The sales order sells the commercial promise; the customer project records how the work is delivered.
processes.business_intent: Sell project-based services with a sales order linked to a customer project and bill fixed price, time and expenses, periodic service, usage-based or mixed commercial models.

control_plane.why: connects the commercial contract with project execution and cost collection

control_plane.control: billing method / billing plan item usage
control_plane.why: decides fixed-price, time-and-expense, periodic, usage-based or payment-on-account behavior
separates project execution evidence from final SD billing

data_hinges.changes: whether project-linked sales-order data can be created or changed
how and when billable value is calculated

data_hinges.data: recorded time, expenses and external services
data_hinges.changes: billing basis and project margin for consumption-based models

impact_summary: Physical delivery may be irrelevant; the important downstream evidence is project activity and cost rather than stock movement.
Sales, Project Management, Procurement and Billing share one customer contract but own different execution objects.
constraints: Do not model project services as a normal material order with a few text items; the billing and cost objects are different.
API operations and allowed changes can depend on customer-project stage.
lead_questions: What is the commercial object and what is the execution object?
Which billing model is used and what evidence makes it billable?
Where do external services and procurement costs enter the project margin?

processes.title: Recurring Delivery of Physical Products from Subscription
processes.memory_hook: The customer buys a recurring promise; background orchestration creates the individual sales orders.
processes.deployment_scope: SAP S/4HANA / Service and Solution Business scenarios; documented for 2025/2602-era solution business.
processes.business_intent: Deliver a physical product repeatedly under a subscription-style commercial agreement where delivery-plan lines periodically generate normal sales orders for fulfillment.

control_plane.why: creates the planned delivery lines and dates
controls which plan lines are open, processed or changed
materializes a recurring commercial commitment into executable SD orders

data_hinges.changes: how many delivery-plan lines exist and their dates
the physical order quantity generated for each cycle
which future plan lines are affected without rewriting already processed deliveries

impact_summary: The sales order is a generated execution document, not the long-lived commercial contract.
This pattern is useful when physical goods are part of a subscription or solution bundle.
constraints: Keep subscription lifecycle ownership outside the generated sales order; otherwise contract changes and delivery execution become tangled.
Feature availability and orchestration details are deployment- and release-specific.
lead_questions: Which object is the commercial source of truth: subscription contract or sales order?
How are future delivery dates generated and changed?
What happens to already processed delivery-plan lines when the subscription changes?
